sources.title: 设计动机：按模型、负载与 GPU 交付
sources.excerpt:
Today's engines are million-line programs that carry, in one codebase:

```
models × precisions × GPUs × parallelism × decoding tricks × workloads
```

The two biggest open engines: 1.4M and 2.0M lines, 280 and 247 model files.

Say you only want K3 to be fast on an NVL72. In a shared engine that is a
change to code that also serves every other model on every other GPU, and
there are three ways to make it:

- **Upstream.** Your PR joins 10,000 others open in those two. Four in five
  have no human review.
- **Fork.** Skip rebases and miss every new model and kernel. Take them and
  fight conflicts; even a clean one ships thousands of PRs never run on your
  GPUs.
- **Hand it to an agent.** Which kernel runs? If the arch is this, and the
  head count is that, and the dtype is something else, unless parallelism is
  on, or a flag says otherwise. Good luck.

kern splits engine from model. The engine contains no model and rarely
changes. The model, parallelism included, ships as three things:

```
manifest.json     one typed declaration: buffers, states, ops, programs, parallelism
kernels/          compiled device code, from anywhere
weights           the model's own Hugging Face checkpoint
```

**A model is not code to merge. It is a package you own.**

Your K3-on-NVL72 engine is your repo, like
[kern-k3-pp-prefill](https://github.com/pegainfer-project/kern-k3-pp-prefill).
No review queue, no rebase, no "it depends." For an agent, that repo is the
whole world.

sources.title: 清单可调范围与替换设备代码示例
sources.excerpt:
## Agents change the whole stack

Everything that makes an engine fast lives in the manifest, so it is all
fair game: which kernel runs each op, where the fusion boundaries are, how a
step maps to launches, how the model splits across GPUs, how speculative
decoding composes its rounds.

**Fast.** A changed manifest is type-checked in milliseconds. `kern test`
replays it against a reference span by span and returns a verdict in
seconds. `kern bench` says where the time goes on the shapes your service
actually sees, not on one representative batch.

**Safe.** Zero trust: every kernel is pinned by SHA-256, every buffer it
touches is declared, and nothing ships without a verdict against the
reference. The engine stays the same, so a change can only break the
manifest it lives in.

One line of a manifest can point at a kernel package on the Hugging Face hub:

```diff
  "silu_mul": { "params": ["out buffer<bf16>", "in buffer<bf16>"],
    "impl": { "launches": [{
-     "entry": "_ZN4vllm18act_and_mul_kernel…packed_silu_kernel…",
+     "module": "activation",
+     "entry": "_ZN4vllm18act_and_mul_kernel…",
  "modules": {
+   "activation": { "source": "hf:kernels-community/activation/…/_activation_320b408.abi3.so",
+                   "sha256": "73748b54…b1fe49aa" }
```

A runtime with no torch and no Python fetched it, verified it, ran it.
Output: byte-identical.

sources.title: 模型包与 manifest
sources.excerpt:
kern splits engine from model. The engine contains no model and rarely
changes. The model, parallelism included, ships as three things:

```
manifest.json     one typed declaration: buffers, states, ops, programs, parallelism
kernels/          compiled device code, from anywhere
weights           the model's own Hugging Face checkpoint
```

**A model is not code to merge. It is a package you own.**

Your K3-on-NVL72 engine is your repo, like
[kern-k3-pp-prefill](https://github.com/pegainfer-project/kern-k3-pp-prefill).
No review queue, no rebase, no "it depends." For an agent, that repo is the
whole world.

## Architecture

![kern architecture: your package is verified, then run inside a host or examined by the harness](docs/figures/architecture.svg)

### The manifest

Everything an engine would need to know about a model is written down in the
manifest, so the runtime does not have to know it. A program is a list of
calls. Each call binds an op to buffers and vars, and each op is a typed
signature plus the launches that implement it:

```json
"ops": {
  "embedding": {
    "params": ["in buffer<i64>", "in buffer<bf16>", "out buffer<bf16>", "i32"],
    "impl": { "launches": [{ "module": "embedding", "entry": "kern_embedding_i64_bf16",
                             "grid": ["rows", 1, 1], "block": [256, 1, 1], … }] } } },
"programs": {
  "decode": { "graph": true, "calls": [
    { "op": "embedding", "args": [{"buf": "token_ids"}, {"buf": "embed"}, {"buf": "hidden"}, {"var": "rows"}] },
    … ] } }
```

A module is any compiled device code: vendored from FlashInfer or TRT-LLM,
written by hand, or written by an agent. It is pinned by SHA-256 and fetched
from a path, a URL or the Hugging Face hub. Swapping a kernel means editing
one launch.

**Memory** comes in two kinds, and K3 shows both:

```json
"buffers": {
  "token_ids": { "dtype": "i64",  "shape": ["rows"],       "kind": "input" },
  "embed":     { "dtype": "bf16", "shape": [163840, 7168], "kind": "weight",
                 "bind": [{ "tensor": "language_model.model.embed_tokens.weight" }] },
  "stats":     { "dtype": "i32",  "shape": [224],          "kind": "workspace" }
},
"states": {
  "kv":  { "bytes_per_token": 1152 },
  "kda": { "bytes_per_seq": 19537920 }
}
```

A buffer is a tensor whose kind says where it comes from: the caller
supplies an `input`, a `weight` binds by name to a tensor in the
Hugging Face checkpoint, and `workspace` is scratch that lasts one call.
A state is memory that outlives a step, declared only by its size. K3's MLA
cache takes 1,152 bytes per token and its KDA linear-attention state takes
19.5 MB per sequence. The runtime pages the first and hands out slots of the
second, both from one pool, and never learns that one is attention and the
other a recurrence.

**Shapes** come from vars. `rows` in the shapes and launch grids above is
one, along with sequences and context length, and each has a bound. Every
buffer size and launch grid is checked at those bounds, and a call outside
them is rejected before it launches.

sources.title: runtime、页池、验证工具与宿主
sources.excerpt:
**Parallelism and serving** are declared too. Topology names rank groups,
and a `peer` buffer holds the other ranks' addresses, so an all-reduce or an
all-to-all is a kernel in the manifest. A new parallel layout is a new
manifest, not a runtime change. The serving protocol says which buffers carry
tokens, slots and sequence lengths, and which programs run per batch. Hosts
read those roles and never a model's name.

Because all of this is data, `verify` checks the whole manifest at once in
milliseconds and reports every problem, not just the first. That is the loop
an agent iterates against.

### The runtime

`kern-runtime` loads a verified manifest, allocates, binds weights, lowers
each program to a flat launch list and replays it, captured as a CUDA graph
per shape bucket where it can. The binary links no CUDA library; it dlopens
the driver and cuBLAS on first use. Nothing in it branches on a model.

`kern-pool` makes every decision about state memory as pure host code and
returns it as a plan the runtime executes, so the bookkeeping is tested
without a GPU. It does two things.

![kern-pool page sharing: a lease writes its pages, retiring freezes them in place as a checkpoint, and a request with the same prefix shares the whole pages and copies only the partial one](docs/figures/pool.svg)

**It shares prefixes by page.** A request leases the pages its worst case
needs and a state slot, all or nothing. When it ends, its pages freeze in
place as a checkpoint. A later request with the same prefix shares the
whole pages and gets a copy of only the page the prefix ends inside, so
every page has at most one writer. A token radix tree finds the longest
checkpoint for a prompt; under pressure, the checkpoint worth least is
dropped.

**Its pages and slots are fixed at load.** Every pooled state is one VMM
allocation sized once from the capacity the caller names: so many tokens
of pages and so many sequence slots. Leasing and freeing touch only free
lists, and a lease short of a page or a slot waits (`Busy`) for the
scheduler to make room by parking or dropping a kept prefix. Nothing is
remapped, so a state's address never changes, the same allocation can be
exported to ranks on other trays, and a prefill tier's mirror of a decode
rank's pool is right for as long as the rank serves. The manifest's `seqs`
bound sizes one step's batch; how many sequences hold state is the
caller's capacity, not a number the manifest fixes.

### The harness

`kern test` takes a reference manifest A and a candidate B. It diffs them
call by call, then records A on a seeded workload, keeping each span's
inputs and the bytes it wrote. B replays span by span from A's own inputs,
so each comparison covers exactly one span's write set, against a noise
floor measured by replaying A against itself. End to end it compares logits
by per-row KL and tells near-ties from real flips by the top-1/top-2 margin.
The verdict is one line and an exit code: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 inconclusive.

`kern bench` takes a workload of shapes (sequences × rows × context) and
attributes time to every call inside the real program; `--isolate` measures
a single call on its own, cold and warm. A server's traced steps become a
workload directly, so a change is priced in GPU seconds on the traffic
actually served. `kern cut` slices a manifest into pipeline stages by
liveness, each stage a manifest whose inputs are the previous stage's
outputs.

Everything is deterministic: no clocks, no randomness, no dependence on
iteration order. The same manifest and inputs give the same bytes, so
running twice and diffing is a test.

### Hosts

`kern-serve` is kern's own server: continuous batching, an OpenAI-compatible
API, a prefix cache, sessions that sleep to host memory, and EP, TP and
pipeline stages across trays. kern also runs as the model inside vLLM or
SGLang: the host allocates the KV and state pools, kern checks their layout
against the manifest's `host` states, and launches enqueue on the host's
stream, inside its CUDA graphs. Scheduling, caching and sampling stay with
the host; the forward pass is the manifest.

Details: [manifest](docs/manifest.md) · [runtime](docs/runtime.md) ·
[pool](docs/pool.md) · [test](docs/test.md) · [bench](docs/bench.md) ·
[serve](docs/serve.md) · [vLLM](docs/vllm.md) · [SGLang](docs/sglang.md)

sources.excerpt:
# kern-llm

[kern](https://github.com/pegainfer-project/kern) runs a model as a manifest: a typed declaration of
buffers, states, ops and programs, compiled kernels, and weights. This package is kern for Python:

- `kern`: the runtime binding (`kern.Runtime`), the readers of a manifest's host contract
  (`kern.host`) and the rank group over `torch.distributed` (`kern.group`);
- `kern_vllm`: a vLLM plugin that runs a manifest as the model;
- `kern_sglang`: the same for SGLang.

```bash
pip install kern-llm
hf download Pegainfer/kern-qwen38-sm103 --local-dir kern-qwen38
KERN_MANIFEST=kern-qwen38/manifests/qwen3.8-27b-vllm.json KERN_KERNELS=kern-qwen38/cubins \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --hf-overrides '{"architectures": ["KernForCausalLM"]}' \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-prefix-caching \
  -cc '{"mode": 0, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

Linux x86_64 and aarch64, Python 3.10 or newer. The runtime loads the NVIDIA driver (CUDA 13, r580 or
newer) and cuBLAS 13 when it first runs; torch comes from the engine. The plugins do nothing unless
`KERN_MANIFEST` is set. Guides: [vLLM](https://github.com/pegainfer-project/kern/blob/master/docs/vllm.md),
[SGLang](https://github.com/pegainfer-project/kern/blob/master/docs/sglang.md).

sources.title: 注册架构
插件具名契约
sources.excerpt:
"""`KernForCausalLM`: vLLM's model slot, filled by a kern runtime.

The manifest contract, read from the manifest and nothing else:

- a host state per cache layer, `<kind>.l<i>` for model layer i: a rank-4
  `[B, H, N, C]` view is an attention layer, `kv` packing k | v in C, `mla`
  one head of a latent (vLLM's `MLAAttentionSpec`); a rank-2 `[B, bytes]`
  view is a recurrent state page. The layer stubs below turn each into the
  vLLM spec that allocates exactly that view.
- inputs, each copied from vLLM's metadata if the manifest declares it:
  `token_ids`, `positions`, `slot_mapping`, `seq_lens` (the positions this
  rank holds: vLLM's DCP-local lengths under decode context parallelism),
  `cu_seqlens_q`, `block_table` (`[seqs, W]` kernel blocks), and the line
  table indexing the state pages (`[state layers, seqs]`, rows in layer
  order); output `hidden`; `head_in` -> `head` -> `logits`.
- programs `decode_batch` (`seqs` sequences of one row), `head` (`seqs`
  rows of logits), and `once` programs to run after binding; optionally
  `prefill` (`seqs` sequences of any lengths, `tokens` rows in all, split
  by `cu_seqlens_q`). Without it the manifest only decodes, and a prompt
  reaches the cache another way (a KV connector).

A step is split into runs the programs accept: consecutive one-token rows go
through `decode_batch` together, consecutive longer rows through one
`prefill`, so the step's prefill rows share every weight read.
A pure decode step is one `decode_batch` over vLLM's padded batch, so vLLM
can capture it; padded rows have no slot and the null state page, which
the kernels skip. A sequence's first chunk finds its state pages zeroed
here, a one-token prompt's too: vLLM hands out pages without clearing them
and reuses a freed one first.

A manifest with a topology runs one rank per vLLM tensor-parallel rank:
member `i` of every topology group is TP rank `i`. The ranks trade offers
over vLLM's gloo TP group when the model is built; on the first bind they
run the `once` programs and meet at a barrier. `logits` is then this
rank's contiguous slice of the vocab, gathered over the TP group.

Prefix caching runs in vLLM's `align` mode: a sequence holds a state page
per block, and the page a step runs on is its last token's block. vLLM
copies the state there from the previous block before the step (a whole
page, `linear_attention_state_copy_func`), so the programs see one page per
sequence, as without caching.

sources.title: 宿主状态与 stub layer
初始化与调度上界
sources.excerpt:
class KernForCausalLM(nn.Module, IsHybrid, SupportsMRoPE):
    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
        super().__init__()
        m = manifest()
        self.m = m
        self.group = get_tp_group().cpu_group if m.get("topology") else None
        self.rt = kern.Runtime(os.environ["KERN_MANIFEST"], os.environ["KERN_KERNELS"],
                               [checkpoint(vllm_config.model_config.model, vllm_config.model_config.revision)],
                               torch.cuda.current_device(),
                               None if self.group is None else group.topology(m, self.group))
        if self.group is not None:
            group.connect(self.rt, m, self.group)
        self.layers = nn.ModuleDict({f"l{i}": stub(n, i, h) for n, i, h in host_states(m)})
        self.line_table = line_table(m)
        inputs = [n for n in (*INPUTS, self.line_table) if n in m["buffers"]]
        self.b = {n: region(self.rt, m, n) for n in inputs + ["hidden", "head_in", "logits"]}
        self.errors = {n: region(self.rt, m, n) for n, b in m["buffers"].items() if b.get("fill") == "error"}
        self.check = bool(os.environ.get("KERN_CHECK_ERRORS"))
        tokens, width = self.b["hidden"].shape
        self.tokens = tokens
        s = vllm_config.scheduler_config
        if s.max_num_batched_tokens > tokens or s.max_num_seqs > self.b["head_in"].shape[0]:
            raise ValueError(f"`{m['model']}` runs at most {tokens} tokens of {self.b['head_in'].shape[0]} sequences "
                             f"a step; vLLM schedules {s.max_num_batched_tokens} of {s.max_num_seqs}: lower "
                             "--max-num-batched-tokens / --max-num-seqs")
        self.out = torch.zeros(tokens, width, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
        self.vocab = vllm_config.model_config.get_vocab_size()
        self.vocab_slice = self.b["logits"].shape[1]
        self.decode_rows = resolve(m, m["programs"]["decode_batch"]["batch"]["groups"])
        self.prefill_seqs = resolve(m, m["vars"]["seqs"]["max"])
        self.cache_config = vllm_config.cache_config
        self.bound = None
        self.rope_dims = vllm_config.model_config.mrope_num_dims if vllm_config.model_config.uses_mrope else 1

sources.title: eager 绑定宿主地址
sources.excerpt:
def bind(self) -> None:
        """Bind (again, when vLLM reallocated) the layers' caches."""
        assert not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing(), "kern binds on an eager step, before capture"
        first = self.bound is None
        # vLLM settles the state block size after the model is built.
        self.state_block = self.cache_config.mamba_block_size
        regions = {n: host_region(self.layers[f"l{i}"].view) for n, i, _ in host_states(self.m)}
        self.rt.bind_host(regions)
        logger.info("kern bound %d host states at %#x", len(regions), min(r[0] for r in regions.values()))
        if first:
            group.start(self.rt, self.m, self.group)
        self.state_names = [f"model.layers.{i}.linear_attn" for _, i, _ in state_pages(self.m)]
        self.state_layers = [self.layers[f"l{i}"] for _, i, _ in state_pages(self.m)]
        self.bound = self.layers[next(iter(self.layers))].view

sources.title: 从张量提取地址和布局
vLLM 捕获与跨队列依赖
sources.excerpt:
### 5. CUDA graphs capture the stream, not operators

A builder declares which graphs it can take part in:

```python
class AttentionCGSupport(Enum):
    ALWAYS = 3; UNIFORM_BATCH = 2; UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE = 1; NEVER = 0
```

Under `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` the runner runs each decode batch size once eagerly,
then once inside `torch.cuda.graph`. Anything issued on the current stream
during the forward is recorded, including launches from another stream that
joins through an event fork/join. So kern's launches land in vLLM's graph with
no PyTorch integration.

### 6. vLLM never interprets page contents

The block pool allocates, frees and optionally zeroes whole pages. Only prefix
caching in "align" mode copies state, through copy functions the model
provides. Whether a GDN page uses kern's internal layout or vLLM's is invisible
to vLLM. The only things that must agree are strides and page sizes.

sources.title: 延迟编译、探测缓存和重新绑定
sources.excerpt:
## What kern needed

### Host states in the manifest

A new kind of state: `host` declares memory the host allocates, and the layout
kern's kernels were written against.

```json
"kv.l3":  {"host": {"dtype": "bf16", "shape": [0, 4, 64, 512], "strides": [131072, 512, 2048, 1]}},
"gdn.l0": {"host": {"dtype": "u8",   "shape": [0, 3207168],     "strides": [3407872, 1]}}
```

An outer extent of 0 means any number of blocks. Every other extent and every
stride must match exactly. The verifier rejects host states that also set a
`bytes*` size, malformed layouts (only the outer extent may be 0, no zero
strides, no overflow), and host states used as a peer's `of` or as an
`index_into` target (the host owns the block ids).

### Runtime: load first, compile at bind

```rust
// crates/kern-runtime/src/host.rs
pub fn bind_host(&mut self, regions: &BTreeMap<String, HostRegion>) -> Result<()>;
pub fn enqueue_after(&self, program: &str, vars: &BTreeMap<String, u64>, stream: u64) -> Result<()>;
pub fn region(&self, name: &str) -> Result<(u64, u64)>;
```

- `Runtime::load` allocates weights, buffers and scratch as before, so the host
  can budget its memory around them. A manifest with host states is not
  compiled yet: programs bake addresses into their launch lists, and host
  states have no address until bound.
- `bind_host` takes the host's pointer, dtype, shape and strides per state,
  checks each against the declaration (`HostTensor::admit`), and compiles only
  if all match. Binding again replaces all host states, recompiles and
  destroys the runtime's own captured graphs. vLLM needs this because it
  allocates the KV cache twice: first a small one to measure graph memory, then
  the real one.
- `enqueue_after` records an event on the host stream and makes kern's stream
  wait on it. It then issues the launches, records an event on kern's stream,
  and makes the host stream wait. Both edges are events, so the same call gets
  recorded into a graph the host is capturing.
- `region` returns a runtime buffer's address, so the host writes inputs and
  reads outputs with `copy_` in its own stream order (also valid during capture).

sources.title: 接入 vLLM 的动机与优化闭环
sources.excerpt:
## Summary

A kern manifest can now run as the model inside an unmodified vLLM (MRv2),
loaded through a plugin. vLLM keeps everything outside the forward pass:
scheduling, the KV cache and its block pool, CUDA graphs, sampling, the API
and the profiler endpoint. kern runs the forward pass on memory that vLLM
allocates.

```bash
pip install kern-llm
hf download Pegainfer/kern-qwen38-sm103 --local-dir kern-qwen38
KERN_MANIFEST=kern-qwen38/manifests/qwen3.8-27b-vllm.json KERN_KERNELS=kern-qwen38/cubins \
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --hf-overrides '{"architectures": ["KernForCausalLM"]}' \
  --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --enable-prefix-caching \
  -cc '{"mode": 0, "cudagraph_mode": "FULL_DECODE_ONLY"}'
```

The architecture override selects the plugin's model class instead of
vLLM's Qwen3.8 implementation. The weights still come from the Hugging Face
checkpoint, and the manifest's own bounds cap the scheduler limits.

The point is to close the loop between offline optimization and serving.
Work on kern is judged offline (`kern test` against a reference, `kern bench`
for where time goes), but production traffic runs on vLLM, whose scheduler
builds batches that kern's own loop never sees: chunked prefill mixed with
decode in one step, decode replayed from vLLM's graphs, KV pages handed out by
vLLM's allocator. With the plugin, the manifest that passed the offline gate
is the one serving traffic, so each turn of the loop below starts and ends on
live traffic:

![Serve, sample, locate, optimize, merge, gate](figures/vllm-rsi-loop.svg)

1. **Serve.** A new manifest goes to one canary replica, then out through a
   rolling restart. Rolling back means pointing at the old manifest.
2. **Sample.** The plugin already sees every step's shape (program, tokens,
   seqs, context lengths) in vLLM's metadata. It logs a histogram at
   negligible cost.
3. **Locate.** Step counts × per-shape `kern bench` time gives GPU time by op
   and shape, the workload for the turn. An occasional profiler trace checks
   that the offline numbers still predict online time.
4. **Optimize.** A main agent separates structural work (how a step maps to
   program calls, fusion boundaries) from per-op work. It splits the call
   graph into disjoint regions and hands each to a sub-agent together with
   its shapes and the current outputs as reference.
5. **Merge.** Speedups do not add up, so the main agent folds the results
   into a new base manifest, regenerates the hosted one and benches the whole
   program on the workload.
6. **Gate.** `kern test` covers every shape the manifest declares, not only
   the frequent ones: agents tuned on a histogram tend to regress the tail.

All six steps now run; [vllm-rsi-example.md](vllm-rsi-example.md) is one
night of the loop on this model (17% more requests than stock vLLM, −5.3% GPU
time over three rounds). With `KERN_TRACE=<dir>` the plugin writes one JSON line per step
(`kern_vllm/trace.py`, about 0.2% of a step's CPU time).
`python -m kern_vllm.workload <trace>` buckets the steps into a weighted
`kern bench` workload, and `kern bench` runs the served manifest itself
(`Verified::self_hosted`) and prices the traffic in GPU seconds. On a
5-minute Poisson run (2026-09-26, one GB300) the bench accounts for 294 of
the 308 s the GPU was busy. The shape distribution is also not fixed: a
faster prefill changes how vLLM batches, so each turn samples again, not
reusing the last histogram.

sources.title: forward 的实际分派
sources.excerpt:
def forward(self, input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors=None, inputs_embeds=None, **_):
        n = input_ids.shape[0]
        positions = positions[0] if positions.dim() == 2 else positions
        meta = get_forward_context().attn_metadata
        cache = self.layers[next(iter(self.layers))].view
        if not meta or cache.numel() == 0:
            return self.out[:n]
        if self.bound is not cache:
            self.bind()
        if any(k not in meta for k in self.state_names):
            return self.out[:n]
        attn = next(meta[k] for k in meta if k.endswith(".attn"))
        states = [meta[k] for k in self.state_names]
        lines = self.lines(states, attn)
        stream = torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream
        if attn.max_query_len == 1:
            # A one-token prompt's first step is a decode row. vLLM runs a step holding a prompt
            # eagerly, never from a decode graph, so a graph never meets a fresh row.
            if not torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
                self.zero_fresh(attn, states)
            for r0, r1 in chunks(0, attn.num_reqs, self.decode_rows):
                self.run(stream, "decode_batch", input_ids, positions, attn, lines, r0, r1, r0, r1)
            return self.out[:n]
        if "prefill" not in self.m["programs"]:
            raise NotImplementedError(
                f"`{self.m['model']}` only decodes (no `prefill` program), but a step has rows of up to "
                f"{attn.max_query_len} tokens: fill the prompt's cache with a KV connector")
        self.zero_fresh(attn, states)
        qsl = attn.query_start_loc_cpu.numpy()
        for r0, r1 in runs(np.diff(qsl[: attn.num_reqs + 1]), self.decode_rows, self.prefill_seqs, self.tokens):
            program = "prefill" if qsl[r1] - qsl[r0] > r1 - r0 else "decode_batch"
            self.run(stream, program, input_ids, positions, attn, lines, r0, r1, int(qsl[r0]), int(qsl[r1]))
        return self.out[:n]

sources.excerpt:
"""A manifest's ranks, one per process, over a `torch.distributed` group.

An engine already has a process group spanning the ranks (vLLM's and
SGLang's tensor-parallel group, each with a gloo `cpu_group`); kern rides
it instead of a channel of its own. `connect` gathers every member's offer
and maps the peers; `start` runs what the manifest runs once and then waits
for every member, because a rank that ran its setup must not push into a
peer whose setup (a Lamport stage poisoned to -0.0, say) has not run yet:
the poison would overwrite what arrived and the reader would wait forever.

The group spans every topology group of the manifest, member `i` of it
being member `i` of each; a manifest whose groups are smaller than the
world needs a group per topology group, which no engine asks for yet.
"""
import torch.distributed as dist

from kern.host import once


def topology(m: dict, group) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]] | None:
    """This process's place in every topology group of `m`, as `kern.Runtime` takes it:
    its rank in `group`, whose size each topology group must be. None without a topology."""
    groups = m.get("topology", {}).get("groups")
    if not groups:
        return None
    me, world = dist.get_rank(group), dist.get_world_size(group)
    wrong = {g: n for g, n in groups.items() if n != world}
    if wrong:
        raise ValueError(f"process group of {world} ranks; the manifest's topology groups of other sizes: {wrong}")
    return {g: (me, world) for g in groups}


def connect(rt, m: dict, group) -> None:
    """Gather every member's offer over `group` and connect `rt` to them all."""
    me, world = dist.get_rank(group), dist.get_world_size(group)
    groups = m.get("topology", {}).get("groups", {})
    wrong = {g: (rt.rank(g), n) for g, n in groups.items() if (rt.rank(g), n) != (me, world)}
    if wrong:
        raise ValueError(f"process group rank {me} of {world}; the runtime's (index, size) per group: {wrong}")
    offers = [None] * world
    dist.all_gather_object(offers, rt.offer(), group=group)
    rt.connect({g: offers for g in groups})


def start(rt, m: dict, group=None) -> None:
    """Run the manifest's once programs, then wait at `group`'s barrier."""
    for name in once(m):
        rt.run(name, {v: 1 for v in m.get("vars", {})})
    rt.synchronize()
    if group is not None:
        dist.barrier(group=group)

sources.title: Verifier 范围与信任边界
sources.excerpt:
## Verifier（`kern-manifest`）

`verify()` 收集全部错误一次报告（`VerifyErrors`）：

1. `schema_version`；
2. var `max ≥ 1`；
3. state 恰有 `bytes_per_token` / `bytes_per_seq` / `bytes` 之一非零；
4. buffer shape 解析、字节数在 var 上界下不溢出；`fill`（若有）落在
   input / output 的 i32 / i64 buffer 上，input 角色对 input、output 角色
   对 output；domain（若有）自洽：
   界的类型对得上 dtype、`index_into` 指向存在的 buffer/state、
   `index_into` 与 min/max 互斥、`monotone` 只许一维、min ≤ max 在
   var 两端成立；
5. module：`sha256` 64 位 hex、`source` 非空、registry ref 语法；
6. op impl 逐 launch：kernel launch 的 `module` 可解析（没有 module 的
   launch 必须是 `extern:` 内置，带 module 的 entry 不得是 `extern:`）；
   block 不超 CUDA 限制、grid 在 var 上界不超 CUDA 限制/下界不为零；launch args 与 launch params（缺省 = 接口）
   数量/逐位类型匹配；
7. impl 与接口的自洽：launch 不得写穿接口 `in` 参、接口 `out` 参必须被
   某个 launch 写到、scratch dtype + 跨 launch 数据流（禁止读未写的
   scratch）、未使用的 scratch 拒绝；
8. call：op 引用、实参与**接口**参数逐位匹配（dtype 精确匹配、state 只
   能接 `state`、var/表达式的取值范围必须装进标量参数类型、offset 对齐
   且在界内）；
9. 逐 program 数据流：禁止读未写（read-before-write）、禁止写 input/
   weight/source；source 只许 `derive` program 读，`derive` program 不碰
   state / input / output / peer、不调 collective；output / carry 必须被**某个** program 写到（prefill 这类只落
   state 的 program 合法地不写任何 output；carry 在每个 program 内视为
   已写——它的生产者是另一个 program）；program 的 `once` 与 `batch`
   互斥，`batch.groups ≥ 1`、`rows` 是 ≥ 1 的常量或已声明的 var（fill 之间
   是否凑成一份 serving 契约是 `Protocol::check` 的事，不在这里）；
10. 拒绝一切未使用的声明（buffer / op / module / state / var / topology
    group；`shard` 引用一个组也算用到它）；
11. 多卡：组大小 > 0；`peer` buffer 必须 `dtype: u64`、shape 恰为
    `[组大小]`、`of` 指向一个 `export` 的 buffer 或一个 state（不能是
    自己、不能是另一个 peer）、`group` 已声明、不带 domain、自身不可
    `export`；`of`/`group` 只许出现在 peer 上；peer 对 op 只读且视为初始
    已写；`{"rank": g}` 只接 `i32`/`i64` 参且 g 已声明；**带 extern launch
    的 op 不得收到 peer buffer**——runtime 内置（cublasLt）永远不碰 peer
    内存；`cut` 有 id、`stages ≥ 2`、`stage < stages`；
12. pack / tensormap / cluster：`bytes<n>` 只许作 launch 参（不进 extern）、
    只接 `{"pack"}` 实参且 `size == n`，字段都在 image 内、互不重叠，引用的
    接口参 / scratch / var / group 都存在；引用 `out` 接口参的指针字段算
    该 launch 写了它。tensormap 字段宽 128、偏移 64 对齐、只能描述接口上
    的 buffer 或 state 参；维数 1–5、`strides` 比 `dims` 少一且为 16 的正
    倍数、`box` 每维 1..=256、内层 box 字节数是 16 的倍数且不超过 swizzle
    跨度、`dims[0]` 字节数是 16 的倍数、只有最外层维可为 0（铺满）；描述
    符寻址的字节数（末元素之后）在每个 call 上不得超过 `buffer 字节数 −
    offset`（var 上界；铺满的维不算），`out` 参上的描述符算写了它。`cluster`
    无零维、不超 16 块，grid 在 var 上下界都被它整除。
13. shard：组已声明；`by: position` 只在 paged state 上、`by: heads` 只在
    per-seq state 上；一个 paged state 按位置切，则所有 paged state 都按
    位置切、同一个组，且没有 `axis: ranks` 的 var、没有 `blocks` fill；
    heads 的段非空、每段行数与宽度非零、宽度被组大小整除、总字节 = 组大小
    × `bytes_per_seq`。每条都单独报出 state 名、期望值与实际值。

反序列化层已拒绝：未知字段（包括实参对象里的未知键）、重复名字、非法
参数类型串。

**信任边界**：verifier 证明的是"声明自洽"，不是 kernel 行为。谎报自己
读写范围的 cubin 在边界之内被信任（debug 路径可用 compute-sanitizer 兜
底）。加载 cubin 后用 `cuFuncGetParamInfo` 比对参数个数/字节布局属于
runtime crate 的 phase-2 校验。唯一一条 runtime 替 verifier 查的 kernel
行为：**收到 peer buffer 的 launch 在装载时被 `cuobjdump -sass` 反汇编，
任何搬内存的 multicast 指令（`UTMALDG/UTMASTG/UTMAREDG.*.MULTICAST`、
`UBLKCP/UBLKRED.*.MULTICAST`）都拒绝**——multicast TMA 打到 peer/fabric
地址会把发起的 GPU 卡死到整机重启（GB300 实测），而 verifier 看不见
SASS。簇内 barrier 的 `UTCBAR.2CTA.MULTICAST` 不碰全局内存，放行
（MegaMoE 用它）。没有 cuobjdump 就拒绝装载。

sources.excerpt:
"""The Qwen3.8-27B manifest on vLLM's memory.

Rewrites `examples/qwen3.8-27b.json` into a manifest a vLLM model runner
drives (`kern_vllm`): the KV cache and the GDN states become host
states, one per layer, laid out the way vLLM's hybrid allocator lays them
out, and the programs stop at the hidden states, since vLLM samples. The
tables index them as vLLM's ids do: 64-token blocks of every attention
layer, one page per sequence of every GDN layer, so a tool that is its own
host (`kern bench`) can provision them.

vLLM gives every layer of a hybrid model one page per block, the same size
for the attention and the GDN groups: a GDN line (conv [3][10240] bf16,
then [48][128][128] f32) rounded up to whole 64-token attention pages
(TRTLLM-GEN's P64), 832 tokens. An attention layer's view of it is 13
kernel blocks of [64 tokens][4 heads][k | v] (vLLM's LBNHC); a GDN layer's
is one line at the start of the page. Only strides change: the kernels
already take them as arguments or tensormap fields, except the captured
prefill conv, which baked the line stride in and is replaced by
`gdn_conv_fwd`, pinned by sha; its source and cubin are published with
the manifest in `Pegainfer/kern-qwen38-sm103` (`sources/`, `cubins/`).

`prefill` takes a ragged batch: `seqs` sequences of any lengths, `tokens`
rows in all, split by `cu_seqlens_q`, so a step's prefill rows are one
call. The GDN chunk kernels already index chunks through
`fla.chunk_indices` / `fla.chunk_offsets`; `fla_chunk_index` builds those
from `cu_seqlens_q` at the start of every call, and the chunk kernels'
grids cover the bound ceil(tokens / 64) + seqs, the entries past the
call's chunks naming rows nobody owns.

    python tools/qwen38_vllm.py [--input examples/qwen3.8-27b.json] --output qwen3.8-27b-vllm.json [--sampled]

`--sampled` keeps the base's head and sampling after the final norm: vLLM
never runs it, `kern test` gates on it.
"""
import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
from kern_manifest import normalize, resolve_constants  # noqa: E402
from qwen_constants import name_constants  # noqa: E402

LAYERS = 64
ATTN_LAYERS = [l for l in range(LAYERS) if l % 4 == 3]
GDN_LAYERS = [l for l in range(LAYERS) if l % 4 != 3]
KV_HEADS, HEAD_DIM, BLOCK = 4, 256, 64
KV_TOKEN_BYTES = KV_HEADS * 2 * HEAD_DIM * 2
KV_BLOCK_BYTES = BLOCK * KV_TOKEN_BYTES
GDN_DIM, GDN_WIDTH, QKVZ_WIDTH = 10240, 4, 16384
QKVZBA_WIDTH = QKVZ_WIDTH + 96
HIDDEN, MLP_WIDTH = 5120, 17408
GDN_LINE_BYTES = (GDN_WIDTH - 1) * GDN_DIM * 2 + 48 * 128 * 128 * 4
PAGE_BYTES = -(-GDN_LINE_BYTES // KV_BLOCK_BYTES) * KV_BLOCK_BYTES

OLD_KV_PAGE_BYTES = len(ATTN_LAYERS) * KV_BLOCK_BYTES
OLD_GDN_LINE_BYTES = 3211264
MAX_SEQS = 128
CONV_SHA256 = "98b86305a3d49a0b930c6bbbed3f981417b6a7eda584e8645ee4cd51136c9f59"
CHUNK_INDEX_SHA256 = "f6710e1540f0916e2cefc5249d9d928c79b0d1154a2fcbc3885861eff31f9df3"
# chunk_h.cu -DNW=4 -DST=3 -DLINE with a sequence's state line indexed by head alone
CHUNK_H_SHA256 = "e213c16337a8d9caaf5888407ee0b8a3d9227559d434eafd35b74098e6936bdd"
# solve_tril.cu storing whole rows: a ragged call moves a row's place in its chunk, so the zeros above
# the diagonal blocks recompute reads can no longer be left to an untouched workspace
SOLVE_TRIL_SHA256 = "45e872b7d3f13ded775bb16fb0485808ce029dbf2966d52a34b4ec13c083c849"
# line_copy.cu with one sequence per grid row, for the FLA chunk kernels that take h0 by pointer
LINE_COPY_SHA256 = "9eb23dab7d156d3a73183e36bb129ebd8b7fef169e2c8de179e62636bbb711b1"

def layer_of(call):
    return int(call["label"].split(".")[0][1:])


def host_states():
    kv = {"dtype": "bf16", "shape": [0, KV_HEADS, BLOCK, 2 * HEAD_DIM],
          "strides": [KV_BLOCK_BYTES // 2, 2 * HEAD_DIM, KV_HEADS * 2 * HEAD_DIM, 1]}
    gdn = {"dtype": "u8", "shape": [0, GDN_LINE_BYTES], "strides": [PAGE_BYTES, 1]}
    return ({f"kv.l{l}": {"host": kv} for l in ATTN_LAYERS} |
            {f"gdn.l{l}": {"host": gdn} for l in GDN_LAYERS})

sources.title: 记录 metadata，非 GPU 时间戳
sources.excerpt:
"""Every step's shape as vLLM schedules it, one JSON line per step.

Off unless `KERN_TRACE` names a directory. Lines go to
`<dir>/<manifest sha12>.jsonl`, since a new manifest changes how vLLM
batches and the two distributions must not mix:

    {"t": <unix ns>, "q": [query len per request], "s": [seq len per request]}

`t` is when vLLM built the step's metadata. With async scheduling that
happens while the previous step runs, so a step's duration is the interval
between the next two lines, not between its own and the next.

The builder calls `step`, not the model: under full CUDA graphs vLLM
replays decode without calling the model, but builds metadata every step.
The calling thread only enqueues; encoding and writing happen on a listener
thread. Files rotate at `KERN_TRACE_MAX_BYTES` (256 MiB), rotated files are
gzipped, and `KERN_TRACE_FILES` (20) of them are kept.
"""
import atexit
import functools
import gzip
import hashlib
import json
import logging
import logging.handlers
import os
import queue
import shutil
import time


class _Enqueue(logging.handlers.QueueHandler):
    def prepare(self, record):
        return record


class _Line(logging.Formatter):
    def format(self, record):
        return json.dumps(record.msg, separators=(",", ":"))


def _gzip(src: str, dst: str):
    with open(src, "rb") as f, gzip.open(dst, "wb") as g:
        shutil.copyfileobj(f, g)
    os.remove(src)


@functools.cache
def _log() -> logging.Logger | None:
    root = os.environ.get("KERN_TRACE")
    if not root:
        return None
    sha = hashlib.sha256(open(os.environ["KERN_MANIFEST"], "rb").read()).hexdigest()[:12]
    os.makedirs(root, exist_ok=True)
    file = logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler(
        os.path.join(root, f"{sha}.jsonl"),
        maxBytes=int(os.environ.get("KERN_TRACE_MAX_BYTES", 256 << 20)),
        backupCount=int(os.environ.get("KERN_TRACE_FILES", 20)))
    file.namer = lambda name: name + ".gz"
    file.rotator = _gzip
    file.setFormatter(_Line())
    q = queue.SimpleQueue()
    listener = logging.handlers.QueueListener(q, file)
    listener.start()
    atexit.register(listener.stop)
    log = logging.getLogger("kern_vllm.trace")
    log.propagate = False
    log.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    log.addHandler(_Enqueue(q))
    return log


def step(meta):
    """Records one step; padded rows (seq len 0) are left out."""
    log = _log()
    if log is None or meta.seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound is None:
        return
    cu = meta.query_start_loc_cpu.tolist()
    rows = [(b - a, s) for a, b, s in zip(cu, cu[1:], meta.seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound.tolist()) if s > 0]
    log.info({"t": time.time_ns(), "q": [q for q, _ in rows], "s": [s for _, s in rows]})

sources.title: 离线 workload 的分组与过滤
sources.excerpt:
"""A step trace (`trace.py`) as a weighted `kern bench` workload.

    python -m kern_vllm.workload <trace.jsonl> [--samples 16] [--seed 0] > workload.toml

A step is the program calls the model makes of it: its one-token rows
together, one sequence each at its previous length, and every longer row
alone. Calls are counted into buckets, and each bucket becomes one shape
weighted by its count, so `kern bench` prices the traced traffic.

A decode call's sequence count rounds up to vLLM's CUDA graph sizes, which
is what a pure decode step runs at; its context is the mean previous
length. Lengths and prefill rows round to the nearest half octave, but no
sequence grows past the longest one traced, which the server's limit bounds.

vLLM's warmup and graph-capture batches repeat one (query, seq) pair across
every row or decode from nothing; they are left out.
"""
import argparse
import collections
import json
import math

GRAPH_SIZES = [1, 2, 4] + list(range(8, 257, 8))


def dummy(step: dict) -> bool:
    rows = list(zip(step["q"], step["s"]))
    return (len(rows) > 1 and len(set(rows)) == 1) or any(q == s == 1 for q, s in rows)


def calls(step: dict) -> list[tuple[int, int, list[int]]]:
    """(sequences, rows per sequence, previous length per sequence)."""
    rows = list(zip(step["q"], step["s"]))
    decode = [s - 1 for q, s in rows if q == 1]
    return ([(len(decode), 1, decode)] if decode else []) + [(1, q, [s - q]) for q, s in rows if q > 1]


def half_octave(n: float) -> int:
    return 0 if n < 1 else round(2 ** (round(math.log2(n) * 2) / 2))


def bucket(call: tuple[int, int, list[int]], longest: int) -> tuple[int, int, int]:
    groups, rows, context = call
    if rows == 1:
        return next(g for g in GRAPH_SIZES if g >= groups), 1, min(half_octave(sum(context) / len(context)), longest - 1)
    rows = min(half_octave(rows), longest)
    return 1, rows, min(half_octave(context[0]), longest - rows)


def workload(steps: list[dict], samples: int, seed: int) -> str:
    live = [s for s in steps if not dummy(s)]
    longest = max(n for s in live for n in s["s"])
    counts = collections.Counter(bucket(c, longest) for s in live for c in calls(s))
    body = [f"[[sweep]]\ngroups = [{g}]\nrows = [{r}]\ncontext = [{c}]\nweight = {n}\n"
            for (g, r, c), n in sorted(counts.items())]
    return "\n".join([f"# {sum(counts.values())} calls in {len(counts)} buckets",
                      f"samples = {samples}", f"seed = {seed}", ""] + body)


def main():
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    p.add_argument("trace")
    p.add_argument("--samples", type=int, default=16)
    p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    a = p.parse_args()
    print(workload([json.loads(l) for l in open(a.trace)], a.samples, a.seed), end="")

## Results

2026-09-25, one GB300, vLLM `e97573215`. Both servers use the same scheduling
limits. Native vLLM runs its defaults: torch.compile, FULL_AND_PIECEWISE graphs,

  margin is ≤ 0.25 (7 exact ties), which is bf16 noise from cuBLAS picking

sources.title: 后续在线优化结果（reported）
sources.excerpt:
# An optimization loop on vLLM + kern: Qwen3.8-27B

**Interactive page: [kern-baa.pages.dev/rsi](https://kern-baa.pages.dev/rsi/)**, every
measurement the agents took over the night.

## Summary

[vllm.md](vllm.md) runs a kern manifest as the model inside vLLM and sketches
a loop that improves it from live traffic. This note is that loop, run for one
night (2026-09-25 → 26) on Qwen3.8-27B, one GB300.

Every round does the same thing. vLLM serves an hour of agent traffic, and
the step shapes it scheduled become a kern bench workload. Three agents spend
two hours each on the most expensive ops. What passes the gate is merged and
served in the next hour. Three rounds ran, and then the loop was stopped by
hand once round 3's agents were finding about 0.1% each.

![Three servers, one hour of agent traffic each](figures/vllm-rsi-aiperf.svg)

Side by side, with the same vLLM, scheduler limits and traffic:

- **Against stock vLLM**, the optimized manifest served **17% more requests**
  and 15% more output tokens per second, at 27% lower inter-token latency.
- **Against kern's own starting manifest**, the loop cut the GPU time of the
  same traffic by **5.3%** (+5.7% requests online).

## Why the bench stands for production

The loop never optimizes against a synthetic benchmark. Its benchmark is the
served hour, re-sampled every round:

- **The shapes are vLLM's.** The plugin logs every step exactly as vLLM
  scheduled it, including chunked prefill mixed with decode, and batch sizes set
  by real arrivals. A round's workload is those steps counted into buckets.
- **The prices are kern's.** `kern bench` runs the served manifest itself on
  each bucket's shape, with real weights and real context lengths, and
  multiplies by the count. The result is GPU seconds for the hour.
- **It adds up.** On a 5-minute check the bench accounted for 294 of the
  308 s the GPU was busy (the rest is vLLM on the CPU). After round 2 the
  bench predicted −3.1% and the next hour's ITL p50 moved −4.8%.
- **It is stable across traces.** Scoring every deployed manifest on round 3's
  trace reproduces each round's gate result within 0.05 points (table in
  [Results](#results)).

sources.title: 合组 prefill：微基准与服务对照
sources.excerpt:
### Ragged prefill

2026-10-06, one GB300. `prefill` takes `seqs` sequences of any lengths, so
the plugin packs a step's prefill rows into one call (see
`docs/qwen38-vllm.md`). Calling it once per sequence is bit-identical to the
previous manifest (`kern test` PASS at every span); packed and per-sequence
calls agree up to bf16 noise from the GEMM's row count, and greedy output
inside vLLM diverges only at margins ≤ 0.125.

Packed vs one call per sequence, same manifest, empty cache:

| sequences × new tokens | 16×32 | 32×64 | 32×128 | 16×512 | 4×2048 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| speedup | 7.5× | 5.3× | 3.0× | 1.26× | 1.05× |

Each call re-reads the weights (about 12 ms), so the gain is in many short
prefills per step. AgentX replay (`inferencex-agentx-mvp`, seed 20260925),
same kern wheel, per-sequence vs packed:

| concurrency | requests | output tok/s | TTFT p50 ms | steps with ≥ 2 prefill rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 24, 3600 s | 1526 / 1523 | 336.1 / 335.1 | 428 / 421 | 0.08% |
| 64, 1800 s | 306 / 303 | 101.5 / 97.1 | ~115 000 both | 3.8% |

On one GPU AgentX rarely presents the shape: at 24 agents prefills arrive one
at a time, and at 64 the KV pool cannot hold the agents' contexts (cache hit
14%), so steps fill with 8k-token recomputes where packing is worth ~1.05×.

sources.title: 适用边界与接口版本记录
sources.excerpt:
State as of 2026-10-13, vLLM main `12b005eef`, which the plugin now
targets (`get_supported_kernel_block_sizes` takes the spec, DCP asks the
impl whether it can return the LSE); the Qwen3.8 numbers above are from
`e97573215` and have not been re-measured on it:

- **Multi-rank.** A manifest with a topology runs as one rank per vLLM
  tensor-parallel rank. A 4-layer Kimi-K3 decode manifest (3 KDA + 1 MLA,
  TP8 / DCP8 / EP8, Lamport all-reduce, from kern-k3-pp-prefill's
  `k3_vllm.py`) serves over two 4-GPU GB300 nodes, eager and under
  `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs. The manifest has no prefill: one-token prompts
  decode from their first token, longer ones take their cache from vLLM's
  `DecodeBenchConnector`. See
  [Multi-rank: Kimi-K3 decode](#multi-rank-kimi-k3-decode).

The rest of this note explains why vLLM's model interface can host an external
runtime at all, then what kern needed on its side.

sources.title: 宿主插件限制
sources.excerpt:
## Limits

- **Mixed steps.** A step's consecutive prefill rows share one `prefill` call
  and its decode rows one `decode_batch`; a mixed step is still two calls or
  more, run eagerly.
- **Prefix caching** runs in vLLM's align mode at vLLM's block size (832
  tokens here), so up to one block of a cached prefix is recomputed. The
  plugin runs each sequence on its last token's state page; vLLM copies the
  state across blocks. Greedy multi-turn output with and without caching
  agrees up to near-tie flips (top1/top2 margin ≤ 0.125).
- **Ranks are TP ranks.** A manifest with a topology runs one rank per vLLM
  tensor-parallel rank, every topology group the size of the TP group; no
  pipeline parallelism.
- **Decode-only manifests** take a prompt longer than one token only through
  a KV connector.
- **Named contract.** The adapter finds inputs by name (`token_ids`,
  `positions`, `slot_mapping`, `seq_lens`, `cu_seqlens_q`, `block_table`,
  `hidden`, `head_in`, `logits`; the line table by its domain) and programs
  likewise (`prefill`, `decode_batch`, `head`), as documented at the top of
  `crates/kern-py/python/kern_vllm/model.py`. Another model needs a transform that

sources.excerpt:
strides to `bind_host`. On the first bind it also runs the manifest's `once`
   programs, then waits at a barrier of the TP group's gloo `cpu_group` (a
   manifest with a topology joined its peers when the model was built:
   `kern.group.connect` over that group).
3. **Splits each step into program calls.** A pure decode step is one
   `decode_batch`, which is what vLLM captures. In a mixed step, consecutive
   single-token rows go through `decode_batch` together and each prefill row
   through its own `prefill` call. Each call copies the inputs the manifest
   declares from vLLM's metadata into kern's regions (`seq_lens` from the
   DCP-local lengths when vLLM shards the KV), calls `enqueue_after`, and
   copies `hidden` back into vLLM's output buffer. A manifest without
   `prefill` refuses a step with a longer row; its prompts come through a KV
   connector. New requests get their state pages zeroed first, because vLLM
   does not clear them (it hands a freed page out first) and kern's kernels
   always read an initial state. That includes a one-token prompt, whose first
   step is a decode row; vLLM runs a step that holds a prompt eagerly, so the
   zeroing never sits in a graph. The line table (the input whose domain
   indexes the state pages) is built from each state group's block table
   column 0; padded rows (`seq_len = 0`) point at the null page.
4. **Computes logits.** It writes the sampled rows into `head_in`, runs `head`,
   and returns `logits` to vLLM's sampler. Logits narrower than the vocab are
   this rank's contiguous slice of it, gathered over the TP group
